html:
The Battle of Posada was fought in November 1330 in a narrow pass of the southern Carpathians, where the Wallachian voivode Basarab I ambushed and destroyed the army of King Charles I of Hungary.

Charles had marched into Wallachia to punish Basarab for acting as an independent ruler. On the way back his army was trapped in a gorge, where the Wallachians rolled rocks and shot arrows down on it for days. The king barely escaped in disguise. The victory made Wallachia the first independent Romanian state, ruled by Basarab's family for generations. The battle is shown in the Illuminated Chronicle, a Hungarian manuscript. The exact place is still debated. Moldavia followed in the 1360s under Bogdan.
sum: The Battle of Posada was fought in November 1330 in a narrow pass of the southern Carpathians, where the Wallachian voivode Basarab I ambushed and destroyed the army of King Charles I of Hungary.
